description:
# 🐛 Bug-fix PR


## 📌 Summary
Following fixes in PR #1537 and closes #1327.

`X_FRAME_OPTIONS=""` the variable as empty string is often setting 'none' as the value for `frame_ancestors` triggering the else block in security_headers.py
Updated empty string to "ALLOW-ALL" for allowing all `frame_ancestors`.


## 🐞 Root Cause
The issue was triggered by the use of an empty string (X_FRAME_OPTIONS="") as the value for the X_FRAME_OPTIONS header. When this environment variable is set to an empty string, it was being interpreted as 'none' for frame-ancestors in the security headers, which caused the else block in the security_headers.py file to trigger. This resulted in restrictive behavior for frame-ancestors, which could break functionality that relies on iframe embedding.

## 💡 Fix Description

To resolve the issue, the empty string (X_FRAME_OPTIONS="") was updated to "ALLOW-ALL". This change ensures that the frame-ancestors directive is set to *, which allows for embedding from any origin (http, https, and file). The updated value also ensures compatibility with the logic in security_headers.py, where the frame-ancestors value is set correctly.

| Check | Command | Status |
|-------|---------|--------|
| Manual curl test - empty | `X_FRAME_OPTIONS="ALLOW-ALL"` → curl shows `frame-ancestors * file: http: https:` | :white_check_mark: pass |
